caption: The drawing features a detailed depiction of a round, brass or bronze-colored maritime compass with a coppery and aged patina. The upper portion shows a top view of the compass bowl, which is circular, with a rim that has a weathered appearance. Inside the bowl is a detailed compass rose with cardinal directions (“N,” “S,” “E,” “W”) as well as intermediate points (“NE,” “NW,” “SE,” “SW”) in black and white alternating triangular segments. At the center of the compass rose is a circular label with the text "ROBERT MERRILL NEW YORK." The compass needle is depicted as a gold or brass-colored pointed bar, with a central fixing point. On the left and right sides of the bowl are short cylindrical metal fittings. Below the colored drawing are two technical line drawings in black ink: the left one is a side view of the bowl, and the right one is a bottom view, showing the fittings and the square mounting on the base. The whole composition is within a rectangular border, and the name “MAGNUS S. FOSSUM.” is written at the bottom. The background is plain and beige in color.
title: Ship's Compass
